cards.headline: The breakup album he couldn't joke his way out of
cards.snippet: Sea Change began with the end of Beck's long relationship, and he answered it by dropping nearly everything he was known for: the samples, the wordplay, the irony. Recorded over two months in Los Angeles with producer Nigel Godrich, the album is played live and sung plainly — heartbreak, desolation and solitude with nowhere to hide. It reached No. 8 on the Billboard 200, and 'Lost Cause', its fifth track, became the song listeners carried away from it.
cards.context: Fifth track on Sea Change (Geffen, 2002), Beck's eighth studio album.

cards.headline: A Beck made of paper, falling out of the sky
cards.snippet: 'Lost Cause' was never a full single — it went out as a promo in the UK, Germany and Japan, and still reached No. 36 on Billboard's Alternative Airplay chart. Director Garth Jennings made two videos for it. In the first, an effigy of Beck tumbles slowly out of the sky, a clip produced entirely in Adobe Photoshop; in the second, Beck and his band play the song in footage that keeps speeding up, slowing down and slipping into stop motion. MTV called the song 'sparse and melancholy… embellished with soft brush drumming.'
cards.context: The falling-effigy video is the song's main upload today, with 6.5 million views.

cards.headline: The moment he stops fighting
cards.snippet: After two verses of indictment, the fight goes out of the song. Genius's annotators read the repeated line as its reality check: he knows the relationship cannot be salvaged, so he stops fighting for it — and agrees to the breakup with the bitterness still in his voice.
cards.context: It is the line listeners quote back most; seven comments across the uploads repeat it.

cards.headline: For when you're ready to pick up the pieces
cards.snippet: This is the song to play when you're tired of suffering and ready to try to pick up the pieces, and move on...I've reached that point.
cards.context: The most-liked comment on any of the song's uploads.

replies.author: @iamnoone3040
replies.text: Well good luck with it. Honestly I hope you can. I got there too, but I kept falling no matter what I did. Finally, I had to turn myself off. Lost who I was, a whole life in a landfill. Existence is not life, and I hope you find and feel life; it is irreplaceable. 🙂

replies.author: @stephensealey4677
replies.text: 2 years later... did your life find better avenues since you sat there 2 years ago and seen your turning point? I hope it has. Life is too brief to settle for suffering. Cheers Bobby.

cards.headline: Willie sings it at 91
cards.snippet: In 2024, at 91, Willie Nelson recorded the song for his album Last Leaf on the Tree — Beck's breakup ballad carried by the oldest voice in American music, over two decades after Sea Change. One listener: "When my Dad was dying and I was far away, I asked my Mom to play Willie for him. So Willie sang him into the afterlife. ❤️ That's how special Willie was to him and me."
cards.context: From Nelson's 76th album — a song about giving up, sung by a man who never has.

version.versionLabel: Willie Nelson's cover, from Last Leaf on the Tree (2024)

cards.headline: Ted Danson, on triangle, under a blanket
cards.snippet: In 2002 Beck toured Sea Change with The Flaming Lips as his backing band, and this is them on Late Night with Conan O'Brien — the host holds up the album, and the night's guest, Ted Danson, sits in with the band. One listener: "And of course, Ted Danson is there playing triangle under a blanket."
cards.context: The Flaming Lips were his touring band that fall; the host holds up the album as they play.

version.versionLabel: Live on Late Night with Conan O'Brien (2002)
